title: "Example 03 - Gut microbiome beta diversity"
author: "Sergio Diez-Hermano"

  html_document:
    toc: true

---

This example compares gut microbiome beta diversity between smokers and non-smokers, separately for women and men, and between women and men, separately for smokers and non-smokers.

The original PERMANOVA subsampling results are included as two small CSV files. We keep the original non-rejection counts and parametric fitting, and update only the smoothing to the binomial GAM. **Knitting this file does not repeat the expensive subsampling tests.**

# 1. Read and check the data

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
```

```{r data}
library(similaritystructure)
library(ggplot2)

distfile <- system.file("extdata", "distancias_full.csv",
                        package = "similaritystructure")
metafile <- system.file("extdata", "meta_full.csv",
                        package = "similaritystructure")

betadist <- read.csv(distfile, check.names = FALSE)
betameta <- read.csv(metafile)

# Some metadata IDs use hyphens where the distance matrix uses dots.
# Keep IDs that already match; change only those with a matching dot version.
dist_ids <- colnames(betadist)
missing <- !betameta$sample_id %in% dist_ids
revised <- gsub("-", ".", betameta$sample_id[missing], fixed = TRUE)
matches <- revised %in% dist_ids
betameta$sample_id[which(missing)[matches]] <- revised[matches]

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(dist_ids))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(betameta$sample_id))

rownames(betadist) <- dist_ids
rownames(betameta) <- betameta$sample_id

common_ids <- intersect(rownames(betadist), rownames(betameta))

cat("Samples in distance matrix:", ncol(betadist), "\n")
cat("Samples in metadata:", nrow(betameta), "\n")
cat("Matching sample IDs:", length(common_ids), "\n")

# If any ID is missing, show it instead of silently discarding samples.
if (length(common_ids) != 1011L) {
  cat("Unmatched metadata IDs (first 20):\n")
  print(head(setdiff(betameta$sample_id, dist_ids), 20))
  stop("Expected 1011 matching samples. Check the two input files.")
}

betadist <- as.matrix(betadist[common_ids, common_ids, drop = FALSE])
betameta <- betameta[common_ids, , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(rownames(betadist), rownames(betameta)))

betameta$gender <- factor(betameta$gender, levels = c("Male", "Female"))
betameta$smoker <- factor(betameta$smoker, levels = c("no", "yes"))

# Check the four group sizes (smokers / non-smokers by sex).
table(betameta$gender, betameta$smoker)
```

# 2. Similarity structures

The four comparisons are:

- **Female:** female smokers versus female non-smokers.
- **Male:** male smokers versus male non-smokers.
- **no:** female non-smokers versus male non-smokers.
- **yes:** female smokers versus male smokers.

The original settings were alpha = 0.05, 60 subsample sizes, 300 repetitions, seed = 123456, PERMANOVA with 999 permutations, and **sampling with replacement**. The four values of N_fin were 70, 200, 100 and 100, respectively. With replacement, the evaluated subsample sizes may exceed the number of observed individuals.

The saved empirical curves contain 59 or 60 distinct sizes, due to rounding in the original grid. A new run of the current package may use a slightly different grid and produce different Monte Carlo results.

```{r cached-results}
comparisons <- c("Female", "Male", "no", "yes")
N_fin <- c(Female = 70L, Male = 200L, no = 100L, yes = 100L)

countfile <- system.file("extdata", "betadivers_counts.csv",
                         package = "similaritystructure")
fitfile <- system.file("extdata", "betadivers_fitting.csv",
                       package = "similaritystructure")

counts <- read.csv(countfile)
fits <- read.csv(fitfile)
ss <- list()

for (name in comparisons) {
  empirical <- counts[counts$comparison == name, c("N", "num_nosig")]
  empirical$scaled <- empirical$num_nosig / empirical$num_nosig[1]
  attr(empirical, "num_repet") <- 300L

  # Fit the current binomial GAM to the original 300-test counts.
  smooth <- similaritystructure:::smooth_binomial(
    N_init = 2, N_fin = N_fin[name],
    propsig = empirical, num_repet = 300
  )

  # Reconstruct the original parametric fit from its saved coefficients.
  fitrow <- fits[fits$comparison == name, ]
  raw <- as.numeric(unlist(fitrow[paste0("raw_p", 1:5)]))
  coef <- as.numeric(unlist(fitrow[paste0("ss_p", 1:5)]))
  n <- 2:fitrow$N_fit_max

  fitted <- list(
    vect_N_fit = n,
    fun_fit = (raw[1] + raw[2]*n + raw[3]*n^2 + raw[5]*n^3)*exp(-raw[4]*n),
    Sn = (coef[1] + coef[2]*n + coef[3]*n^2 + coef[5]*n^3)*exp(-coef[4]*n),
    param_Sn = coef,
    Ns_fitting = fitrow$Ns_fitting,
    Gof_fit = fitrow$Gof_fit
  )

  ss[[name]] <- list(scaled_bn = empirical,
                     simil_struct_Ns = list(smooth = smooth, fitting = fitted))
}
```

## Similarity sizes

```{r sizes}
ns <- data.frame(Comparison = comparisons,
                 Fitting = NA_real_, Smoothing = NA_real_)

for (i in seq_along(comparisons)) {
  x <- ss[[comparisons[i]]]$simil_struct_Ns
  ns$Fitting[i] <- x$fitting$Ns_fitting
  ns$Smoothing[i] <- x$smooth$Ns_smooth
}

print(ns, row.names = FALSE, digits = 5)
```

## Empirical curves, fitting and smoothing

Black: scaled empirical non-rejection curve. Red: original parametric fit. Green: updated binomial GAM.

```{r curves, fig.width=12, fig.height=3.5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 4), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

for (name in comparisons) {
  x <- ss[[name]]
  emp <- x$scaled_bn
  fit <- x$simil_struct_Ns$fitting
  sm <- x$simil_struct_Ns$smooth

  plot(emp$N, emp$scaled, type = "l", lwd = 1.5,
       xlab = "Subsample size", ylab = "Scaled beta(n)", main = name)
  lines(fit$vect_N_fit, fit$fun_fit, col = "firebrick", lwd = 1.5)
  lines(sm$vect_N_smooth, sm$fun_smooth, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 1.5)
  abline(v = fit$Ns_fitting, col = "firebrick", lty = 2)
  abline(v = sm$Ns_smooth, col = "darkgreen", lty = 2)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# 3. Normalized similarity structures S(n)

```{r ss-curves, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
colors <- c(Female = "#CC6677", Male = "#4477AA",
            no = "#228833", yes = "#AA3377")

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
max_y <- max(sapply(ss, function(x) max(x$simil_struct_Ns$fitting$Sn,
                                    x$simil_struct_Ns$smooth$Sn)))

for (method in c("fitting", "smooth")) {
  plot(0, 0, type = "n", xlim = c(2, 200), ylim = c(0, max_y),
       xlab = "Subsample size", ylab = "S(n)",
       main = if (method == "fitting") "Parametric fitting" else "Binomial GAM")

  for (name in comparisons) {
    x <- ss[[name]]$simil_struct_Ns[[method]]
    n <- if (method == "fitting") x$vect_N_fit else x$vect_N_smooth
    lines(n, x$Sn, col = colors[name], lwd = 2)
  }
  legend("topright", legend = comparisons, col = colors, lty = 1, bty = "n")
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# 4. Similar effect probability (pS)

We compare the four effects using the current prob_effect() function. The parametric fit is the primary comparison. The GAM is normalized on a finite interval, which can sometimes lead to a zero pS when the other similarity size lies outside its range. Such a zero is a truncation effect, not evidence of an exact population probability of zero.

pS is a descriptive probability, not a hypothesis-test p-value. A threshold such as 0.05 is a user-defined comparison criterion.

```{r ps}
ps_fit <- ps_smooth <- matrix(NA_real_, 4, 4,
                              dimnames = list(comparisons, comparisons))

for (i in 1:3) {
  for (j in (i + 1):4) {
    A <- ss[[comparisons[i]]]$simil_struct_Ns
    B <- ss[[comparisons[j]]]$simil_struct_Ns

    ps_fit[i, j] <- prob_effect(fitting_A = A$fitting, fitting_B = B$fitting)
    ps_smooth[i, j] <- prob_effect(smooth_A = A$smooth, smooth_B = B$smooth)
    ps_fit[j, i] <- ps_fit[i, j]
    ps_smooth[j, i] <- ps_smooth[i, j]
  }
}

cat("pS from parametric fitting:\n")
print(ps_fit, digits = 5)
cat("pS from binomial smoothing:\n")
print(ps_smooth, digits = 5)
```

## pS matrices

The diagonal is left blank because the figure compares different effects.

```{r ps-figure, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
plotdata <- rbind(
  data.frame(as.table(ps_fit), Method = "Fitting"),
  data.frame(as.table(ps_smooth), Method = "Binomial GAM")
)
names(plotdata)[1:3] <- c("A", "B", "pS")
plotdata$A <- factor(plotdata$A, levels = comparisons)
plotdata$B <- factor(plotdata$B, levels = rev(comparisons))

ggplot(plotdata, aes(x = A, y = B, fill = pS)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(pS), "",
                             formatC(pS, digits = 3, format = "g"))), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~Method) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "grey90") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "pS") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# 5. Repeat the analysis (optional)

**Do not execute this block when knitting the example.** It is provided to document the original analysis and rerun the PERMANOVA subsampling if necessary. The supplied counts and parametric fits mean that no expensive recomputation is needed to reproduce the figures.

```{r recompute, eval=FALSE}
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)

for (name in comparisons) {
  if (name %in% c("Female", "Male")) {
    ind1 <- which(betameta$gender == name & betameta$smoker == "yes")
    ind2 <- which(betameta$gender == name & betameta$smoker == "no")
  } else {
    ind1 <- which(betameta$gender == "Female" & betameta$smoker == name)
    ind2 <- which(betameta$gender == "Male" & betameta$smoker == name)
  }

  res <- similarity_structure(
    n1 = betadist[ind1, , drop = FALSE],
    n2 = betadist[ind2, , drop = FALSE],
    N_init = 2, N_fin = N_fin[name],
    num_N = 60, num_repet = 300,
    replace = TRUE, test = similaritystructure::adonis_ss,
    test_args = list(subset_choice = name, permutations = 999),
    alpha = 0.05, seed = 123456, plotting = FALSE
  )

  saveRDS(res, file.path("results", paste0("betadivers_", name, ".rds")))
}
```

The microbiome data originate from curatedMetagenomicData. Sample IDs were normalized from hyphens to dots before matching the metadata to the distance matrix. The corrected data contain **1,011 samples from 10 studies**, not 1,011 independent studies.
